gloss: to be thirsty, to be parched; to thirst for

definitions.gloss: to be thirsty, to be parched
definitions.explanation: To feel thirst. Used with 喉 (throat) in the pattern 喉が渇く. Written with 渇 to distinguish from 乾く (to dry physically).
To strongly desire or crave something, used figuratively.

examples.japanese: {暑|あつ}い{日|ひ}は{喉|のど}が{渇|かわ}きやすい。
examples.english: On hot days, you get thirsty easily.

examples.japanese: {喉|のど}が{渇|かわ}いたので、{自動販売機|じどうはんばいき}で{水|みず}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I was thirsty, so I bought water from a vending machine.

examples.japanese: {愛情|あいじょう}に{渇|かわ}いている。
{知識|ちしき}に{渇|かわ}いた{若者|わかもの}たちが{図書館|としょかん}に{集|あつ}まった。
examples.english: Young people thirsting for knowledge gathered at the library.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY:
{自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive). Pattern: Xが{渇|かわ}く.

ASPECT (ている):
{渇|かわ}いている indicates a current state of being thirsty.

KANJI NOTE:
{渇|かわ}く and {乾|かわ}く are both read かわく but have different meanings. {渇|かわ}く means "to be thirsty" or "to crave," while {乾|かわ}く means "to dry" or "to become dry." In practice, {喉|のど}が{渇|かわ}く and {喉|のど}が{乾|かわ}く are both used for thirst, but {渇|かわ}く emphasizes the craving while {乾|かわ}く emphasizes the physical dryness.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{喉|のど}が{渇|かわ}く (to be thirsty)
・{愛情|あいじょう}に{渇|かわ}く (to crave affection)
・{知識|ちしき}に{渇|かわ}く (to thirst for knowledge)
